title: Wall Street Rebounds as Treasury Yields Ease and Moderna Doubles on Cancer Data
excerpt: U.S. stocks closed modestly higher Wednesday after the Treasury announced expanded buyback operations, cooling a bond-market selloff. Moderna shares more than doubled on promising melanoma vaccine trial results.
body:
• The S&P 500 gained 0.24% to 7,709.91, the Dow rose 0.23%, and the Nasdaq added 0.15% as Treasury yields retreated from multi-decade highs.
  • Moderna shares more than doubled after its personalized mRNA cancer therapy intismeran showed positive late-stage results against melanoma, adding roughly $30 billion in market value.
  • The U.S. Treasury announced it would double the size of liquidity support buyback operations for longer-dated bonds, easing pressure from a multi-day yield surge.
  • Fed minutes from the July meeting revealed deepening inflation concerns, with several policymakers ready to raise interest rates if price growth persists.

Yields Retreat After Treasury Intervention

U.S. stocks snapped a two-day losing streak Wednesday after the Treasury Department threw bond markets a lifeline. The 30-year Treasury yield, which had hit its highest level since 2007 on Tuesday, pulled back alongside the 10-year yield after the government announced it would double the size of liquidity support buyback operations for longer-dated bonds.

The S&P 500 gained 18.15 points to close at 7,709.91. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 123.94 points to 53,467.34, while the Nasdaq Composite added 40.08 points to finish at 26,331.09.

"The risk-on trade is trying to hang on to the lifeline that Treasury Secretary Bessent sent."

— Carol Schleif, Chief Market Strategist, BMO Private Wealth

Schleif noted that riskier assets including high-profile tech stocks had sold off sharply in recent days as bond yields rose, warning that higher rates "could potentially impact the AI trade" as technology companies have been issuing debt and using cash to fund data center construction.

Gains narrowed through the afternoon. Jim Baird, chief investment officer at Plante Moran Financial Advisors, said investors likely took profits after the initial bounce, adding that the Treasury's announcement "doesn't mean that the longer-term issue of higher rates is off the table."

Moderna Doubles on Cancer Vaccine Breakthrough

The session's standout mover was Moderna, whose shares more than doubled to a two-year high of $140.19 after late-stage trial data showed its personalized mRNA cancer therapy cut the risk of melanoma recurrence and spread. The vaccine, intismeran, was developed in partnership with Merck and used alongside Merck's blockbuster immunotherapy drug Keytruda.

The rally added approximately $30 billion to Moderna's market capitalization, with trading volume running at more than 15 times the 50-day average. Merck climbed 10% to an all-time high on the data. Leerink Partners analysts raised their sales projection for the therapy to about $1.4 billion by 2032, up from a prior estimate of $1.2 billion.

The surge rippled across the biotech sector. The Nasdaq biotechnology index rose 4.4% to a fresh record. BioNTech gained 20% and Novavax added 6%. Short sellers in Moderna faced record one-day losses, with short interest at 13.5% of the free float.

"A successful trial gives investors stronger evidence that mRNA technology can have a meaningful future beyond infectious diseases," said Lale Akoner, global market strategist at eToro.

Fed Minutes Show Inflation Anxiety

Minutes from the Federal Reserve's July meeting showed deepening concern over inflation, with "several" policymakers indicating readiness to raise interest rates. "Many" said a rate hike would be necessary if inflation does not decline toward the central bank's 2% target.

Markets largely shrugged off the hawkish tone, focusing instead on the Treasury's buyback announcement. Investors are now watching next week's Jackson Hole symposium for clearer signals on the Fed's policy direction.

Sector Highlights

The S&P 500 healthcare sector hit a record high, providing the biggest boost to the benchmark index. Technology stocks dipped, with the Philadelphia semiconductor index ending lower despite Marvell Technology's 10% gain on its new custom-chip deal with Google.

In retail, Target rose after raising its annual sales forecast, while Lowe's gained despite trimming its full-year outlook. Estée Lauder jumped after forecasting annual profit above estimates.

Oil prices settled higher amid continued Middle East uncertainty. President Trump said no talks were taking place with Iran and insisted the Strait of Hormuz was open, contradicting Iran's claim that the strait remained shut to shipping.
